blog/2025/2025-12-20-2025-12-20-babylon-: Paul names Israel as the ones to whom “the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants” and the promises belong, showing who the “our sakes” of this verse points to. The world was made for Israel, so the agendas of this earth are still about us, even while the heathen devour us.

“Making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit” is business without compassion — the very haggling spirit of the nations. Our statutes had us deal with each other another way, and that is our wisdom in their sight.

This is what wisdom looks like in practice: the one who stole now labours “that he may have to give to him that needeth”. Keeping the statutes means when blessing comes, you give back to your own people instead of only filling your pockets.

Israel once dealt like a merchant with “the balances of deceit” in his hand — a custom picked up from the other nations, not from our law. It shows the opposite of the wisdom that makes nations marvel at us.

The traffic that made Tyrus rich and lifted up her heart was chiefly in people: “they traded the persons of men” along with the brass, oils and precious things. That trade in souls is the wealth behind the boast “I am a God.”

This is the reaping of the whoring Hosea names: because we chased other nations and their ideals, a nation we know not eats “all thy labours,” and we are “only oppressed and crushed alway” — the very curse now falling on the northern kingdom.

Hosea says Ephraim would not dwell in the Lord's land but eat unclean things in Assyria; that is this servitude — serving enemies “in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things,” our resources consumed by others.

Here is the picture of a people held fast and spoiled: “servants upon horses”, those meant to serve us set up in authority, while “princes walking as servants upon the earth” — the sons of God, the truly rich, sitting in low places.

The same holding fast is here: “robbed and spoiled”, snared and hid in prison houses, with “none saith, Restore.” Robbed speaks of our identity taken, spoiled of our lands and resources stripped — which is why our Redeemer must come and plead our cause, since no man will let us go.

Names who this Babylon is, “the glory of kingdoms,” and says her end is “as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah” — never inhabited again. That never happened to the old Babylon, so the sword in Jeremiah 50 is reserved for another time.

Shows what the sword upon the Chaldeans really is: the Lord pleading with all flesh by fire and by his sword, coming “with his chariots like a whirlwind.” The pleading of the redeemer isn't asking politely, it's judgment you can now picture.

Lamentations cries out over our reproach, and Baruch shows what that reproach still looks like: “we are yet this day in our captivity,” scattered and “subject to payments,” bearing our fathers' iniquities. The chains became payments, and we are paying still.

Job says “the earth is given into the hand of the wicked”, which is why the men of Micah 2:1 covet fields and take them by violence — the power is in their hand, and even the judges' faces are covered.

Micah says they do it “because it is in the power of their hand” — and Satan says that power was “delivered unto me” to give to whomsoever he wills. That tells you who hands them the power to devise iniquity and act on it openly.

The reason they can practise iniquity “when the morning is light” is the throne of iniquity “which frameth mischief by a law” — they do it in broad daylight through legislation and institutions, insulated from consequence.

The fall announced here is no accident but judgment: what Babylon dealt out comes back to her “double according to her works.” Assured reciprocity, the recompense that turns the great city into a dwelling of devils, for “strong is the Lord God who judges her.”

Water, fire, iron, salt, flour, honey, milk, wine, oil and clothing are named the principal things needful for life, so when they are targeted and robbed, people are stripped of their dignity. Defrauding the needy of that bread makes “a man of blood” — violence without a sword.
blog/2025/2025-12-20-2025-12-20-christma: Christ warned, “Take heed that no man deceive you,” because many would come in his name saying they are Christ and show great signs and wonders. That is the very deception Paul names here — “another Jesus” preached by men the apostles never sent, so it is right to be on guard rather than bear with him.

Shows who spoils us: the secret counsel of the wicked, who “commune of laying snares privily” — doctrines, philosophies and traditions dug out of Babylon and the old mystic nations, then dressed up in music and advertising to catch our people.

The same command is spelled out wider: every place the nations served their gods must go — high mountains, hills, and “under every green tree”. Not some trees, but every green tree, which is why the groves are cut down.

It tells plainly what the groves were for: “under every green tree, and under every thick oak” was “the place where they did offer sweet savour to all their idols.” The altars, images, and trees all stood together.

It names the very trees of the groves — “under oaks and poplars and elms” — and says the shadow of them is good to those who sacrifice there. It also shows what goes on under that shade: whoredom and adultery.
Shows how far the grove worship went — “enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children”. That is why God wanted those trees cut down, not kept and decorated.

When the heathen “sought to paint the likeness of their images” in the open book of the law, that is the same covering of our faces Job speaks of. The whitewashing of the Hebrews' images is nothing new; the Greeks did it, and the Renaissance revived it.

Edom said “we will return” and build, and here God answers the same way he did in Malachi: however high they rise, as the eagle or with their nest “among the stars,” he says “thence will I bring thee down.” They shall build, but he will throw down.
Christ tells the healed man to “offer the gift that Moses commanded”, showing the gift brought to the altar is a sacrifice. So gifts set under a tree are sacrifices offered at a heathen altar.

“Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise” — the same gifts that belong at the altar are used to buy men's silence. Knowing the gifts under the tree are heathen offerings, they still won't reprove it, because they love the presents.
blog/2025/2025-12-20-2025-12-20-kill-or-: Judgment for mingling with the nations did not fall on the people, priests and Levites right away, so they kept on in their abominations — “the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” The Most High's patience is not approval; the sentence still comes.

The wars and fightings start with loving this world and the things in it, and that love crowds out the love of the Father. Kill that lust inside and the fighting among brothers and sisters dies with it.

Lusting after houses, cars and things to be seen of men makes those things your master, and “ye cannot serve God and mammon.” That divided heart is the adultery and the enmity James is warning you about.

It tells you plainly what the truth is: “thy law is the truth.” So the truth that makes you free in this verse is the commandments of our heavenly father, an everlasting righteousness, and nothing else out here holds it.

Sirach says the wise man “will fear in every thing”, and here is what that fear is: “to hate evil.” Pride, arrogancy, the evil way and the froward mouth are the very things the wise man beholds and loathes, so he will not transgress.
blog/2025/2025-12-21-2025-12-21-jubilee-:
Before Genesis, Deuteronomy 11 was read from verse 21, the word the Lord gave Israel in advance of entering the land: “That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” For us, heaven has always been upon the earth. If Israel would diligently keep the commandments, “Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.” To possess means to own. Then: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours”. Every place your feet touch is your land; that is heaven on earth.

With a map on the screen, verse 24 lays out the borders. “From the wilderness” is the wilderness of Egypt, on the other side of the Nile. “And Lebanon” sits at the top of the map, and Lebanon was ours. “from the river, the river Euphrates” runs through Syria, just above Lebanon. “even unto the uttermost sea” is the Mediterranean on the left. So the land ran from the wilderness of Egypt all the way up to the Euphrates, taking in Syria and everything down from it.

Genesis 15:18 goes with Deuteronomy 11:21-24. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”. The river of Egypt is the Nile. The same land God promised Abraham is the land Israel took. We were fighting from the time of Joshua to get all of it, and we fully had it under David and Solomon.

This matters for Jubilee. Jubilee did not start until Israel got into the land: count seven times seven years, forty-nine, and the fiftieth year is the jubilee, when the land rests and every piece of land goes back to the original owner of that heritage, that tribe. So the land has borders, and they are in the Middle East. The doctrines going around that the Congo, or Kenya, is the real land of Israel cannot stand, because the scripture gives the layout of the land plainly.

From there Isaiah 14 shows the land coming back: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody, only Jacob. We may be at the bottom of society, but he will yet choose Israel, and it is God who sets us in the land, not the League of Nations or the United Nations. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: every nation goes back to the land God first gave it, and “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”. The laws of Leviticus 25 cannot be in effect now while we are the slaves in a foreign land, but when we return to the land they go back into full effect.

The rest the land keeps here was first spoken when “the Lord spake unto Moses in mount Sinai”: when Israel came into the land, it must keep a sabbath. Six years of sowing, then a seventh year of rest, built on the seventh-day Sabbath.

People like to say the Israelites stole the Canaanites' land. We stole nothing; the land was ours, and anything a slave owns belongs to his master. Noah gave the prophecy: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.” Then he is more specific: “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.” Israel comes out of Shem, so the Canaanites shall be the servants of Israel. “God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem”. Whose tents would Japheth be living in? Shem's, the Israelites'. Everything belongs to Shem.

At Genesis 9 there were no twelve tribes yet. Israel does not come into being until Jacob's name is changed in Genesis 32, so Noah speaks in terms of Shem, Ham and Japheth. 2 Esdras 6:54 brings it forward to the chosen people: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Then the part that was wanted, verse 55: “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. God made the world for our sake.

Psalm 82 was read as going with Esdras and Daniel. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Verse 6: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” We are not the Most High, but we are the powers of this earth, the judges of the whole planet. The whole earth belongs to the Israelites.

Verse 5 shows it was always meant to be that way: “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” All means everything. If the Israelites are not ruling the planet with God's commandments and laws, everything is out of line, out of the natural way God made it, and there is gross darkness among the people everywhere else. So Canaan being made a servant is part of God's whole plan: the world was made for the chosen, and everything goes back to them.

After Esdras showed that God made the world for our sakes, Daniel 7:27 gives the next prophecy: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”. What is under the whole heaven is the planet earth. The earth shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.

Psalm 148:14 shows who the saints are: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. Even means indeed: indeed the children of Israel. The Israelites are the saints. Everything on this planet is going back to the Israelites, including the planet itself.

Daniel goes on: “whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Everybody is going to obey Christ. “Hitherto is the end of the matter”: that is the whole plan of God. “As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me”, meaning his thoughts troubled him, “and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.”

This is the end of what began with Noah's words over Canaan. Canaan is a servant of servants and Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem, because the dominion under the whole heaven belongs to Shem's chosen seed. From there the class went to Jeremiah 34 to show what it cost Israel when we disobeyed the year of release and would not let our own brethren go free.

Bondmen were to be bought “of the heathen that are round about you”, not from Israel. A poor brother sold to you serves as a hired servant and goes home at the Jubilee, while those bondmen stayed a possession for ever.
Even after a poor brother is sold, “he may be redeemed again” by a brother, an uncle or a near kinsman. His price was counted by the years left to the Jubilee, just like the land.

The land is the Lord's, so it could never be sold for good: “for the land is mine”. That is why every man returns to his possession at the Jubilee, and land was priced by the harvests left until then.
blog/2025/2025-12-26-2025-12-26-the-king:
“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

Daniel 7:25 is about the white man, about Edom: “he shall speak great words against the most High”. He has called himself the people of God, called himself Christ and the people of Christ, taken God's land, said God's laws are done away with, and changed all of the Most High's holidays. “and shall wear out the saints of the most High”: he wore us out in slavery. When something is worn out it does not look the same, and that is how we forgot who we are.

“and think to change times and laws”. There is a reason it says times. Genesis 1:14: “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The sun and moon are set up for time. The moon is used for time, so that we can tell when our festival days come in.

Times and laws go together. Antiochus changed all our customs and made it unlawful for us to keep festival days, and America did the same thing: you do not have to keep God's feast days any more, why are you keeping Passover or Dedication, Christ did away with those things. In their place came new holidays, Christmas and Easter, our customs twisted and mixed with paganism and fed back to us. There is always a counter, good set against evil: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

It says he will think to change times and laws because he is not going to be able to. The Most High is a mastermind. He has sent his sons, his prophets, back on the earth, and they teach the right times, the feast days and God's laws. The lights he set in the heaven still keep his times.

Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness.” That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day.

Christ says it himself: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” We read that Christ is the first thing created; we go to the first thing created and God says “Let there be light”; and here Christ says, I am that light. The scriptures line up.

That is why the light of Genesis 1:3 is not the light of the sun. The earth was “without form and void”, not yet made, and the sun and moon, the “two great lights”, were not made until “the fourth day.” Read with a carnal mind, it sounds like daylight; read with the spirit, it is the Son.

Moses was told to hide these things and not make them plain for everyone, which is why Christ is called the hidden wisdom. Even the dividing of the light from the darkness, the light called day and the darkness night, is a similitude.

Genesis 1 is an abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel. When Genesis 1:27 says “male and female created he them”, Genesis 2 shows how he did it.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man. “and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: when he breathed into him, he put that spirit inside him, the spirit that is his Son from the beginning. “and man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

Then Eve: “And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Eve was created from Adam, and Adam from the ground.

2 Esdras 3 tells the same story and goes further: God breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could go there, until he sinned. That is why flesh and blood cannot be up there: flesh and blood has that sinful nature. The man who could walk into paradise was not running around naked. He was ruling.

What does it mean when the Lord says, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”? Wisdom of Solomon 2:23: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” That is how Adam was created before he sinned: immortal. Being in God's image is not only about how we look. It goes into his power and his divinity too.

2 Esdras 8:44 says man “is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him, for whose sake thou hast made all things”. Adam was just like his father, the way someone says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. We are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and Christ is in the image of the Father. All things were created for Adam and for the sons of Adam, which is us. Not everyone was created in Adam's image; the sons of God are the ones created in Adam's image, because Adam was created in God's image.

“and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Then in verse 28 God tells them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish means to fill something up again. There is a big gap after verse 27: a lot of time went by. Why would God tell Adam to subdue the earth if he already had dominion over it? That was left to be answered later in the class.

Deuteronomy 11:21 shows Moses saw Adam's kingdom: keep the commandments in the land, and your days will be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam ruled. 2 Esdras 7:26 speaks of the bride that “now is withdrawn from the earth”: that holy city, the access to the spirit realm, withdrew itself from the earth, so it must once have been on the earth, in the time of Adam. How Adam was on the earth is how we are going to be in the future.

“Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day”. This shows when the children of light were created. In Genesis 1 it was not only the light that was created; the light's children were created too. Christ said that he and the children are one. We were already in Christ, and when that light was formed we were in it. Then the Father chose: those on the right side are his children, and those on the left, the two-thirds and the heathen, are the darkness.

God called the light Day, so we are the children of the day. That is why Day and Night are capitalized in the King James: a specific day and a specific night, good and evil, right angels and wrong ones, right spirits and wrong spirits. The apostles understood these things, and the translators did too. “we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” Day and night compare good and evil and the children of each, and all of that took place on the first day.

Paul goes on: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. For God hath not appointed us to wrath”. We should not be sleeping; we have to be aware of the time we are living in. God did not appoint us to wrath because we are the children of the day, the children of the light.

Who is the day? 2 Peter 1:19: “a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place, and the day star arising in our hearts is Christ. He is the day.

2 Esdras 9 shows the children of light before the earth: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed”. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic, celestial bodies, the body we will have when Christ returns, and we all obeyed. “but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”. Covered in this flesh, we became rebellious. Knowing who we were is meant to give us the faith and hope to endure in this truth.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. To be predestinated means you are going to get it no matter what. The definition read was: of an outcome or course of events determined in advance by divine will or fate, with the synonyms preordained, foreordained, destined, predetermined, fated, predestined.

How do you know who is predestined? You don't. Nobody today knows it. When you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know you were predestined. Read on: “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.”

When were we predestined? When God chose to separate the light from the darkness, on the first day. Revelation 13:8 says the same thing from the other side: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. The choosing was done in the beginning, before the earth was made.

“And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.” Moses wrote these things the way God told him to, hiding them so that not everyone would understand. This is the first day, before the earth was created, and the first thing created was Christ. What else was created on that first day?

Isaiah 5:20 names light and darkness plainly: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Darkness is called evil and light is called good. So when the Lord divided the light from the darkness, he created good and evil. Moses is letting us know that something more is going on in Genesis 1.

On that first day spirits were created: angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created. The dividing of the light from the darkness is God choosing. The children of light are his chosen, and the rest he hardens, as the next scriptures show.

“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.” Read on: “His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.” The light stands for good and the darkness for evil, and he separates them with an adamant.

The annotation in the King James gives the meaning of adamant: refusing to be persuaded, or to change one's mind. That is what the hardening of Pharaoh was. God made Pharaoh not be persuaded to let us go. That is the adamant, and that is how God separates his light from the darkness: he hardens a heart so that it will not believe and will not follow. The same way he hardened Pharaoh's heart, he will harden hearts so that people do not believe these scriptures.

So in the beginning, when God separated the light from the darkness, spirits were created, and God said: you I will choose, you are my chosen people; you I will not choose, I will harden your heart. The children of light were chosen, and the darkness was left hardened.

“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything is made in pairs. When God divided the light from the darkness he made good and evil as a pair, and Satan and evil were created too. Nothing got into creation by mistake. There is always a counter, good set against evil all the time: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

Look at what Genesis 1 mentions first, before the earth was formed: the waters of the deep, which is space, covered in darkness. Darkness is mentioned before the light because the Lord had it set from the beginning that, when we came down here, we would be evil anyway.

That is why “the evening and the morning were the first day”: the evening comes before the morning. That is why Cain was born first, Ishmael came before Isaac, and Esau, Edom, was born before Jacob. The evil, the darkness, goes first, and then the light comes after, which is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first. The double of Sirach, darkness set against light, runs through all of Genesis.

“And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.” The waters under the firmament are the sea; the waters above are in space. There are different waters above the firmament: drink that water and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude. “And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.” On the second day the firmament was created, and paradise, which is also called heaven, was created too.

The earth came after. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth”. There was no shape or form down here yet. The earth was made on the third day, with the grass, the herbs and the fruit trees.

2 Esdras 3 confirms the order: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth, so it was made on the second day.

This is why the class kept saying Genesis has levels. When Genesis says God made the heaven, it is not only the sky over this earth. Paradise was planted by God's right hand before the earth appeared, and Adam was led into it.

Our minds are earthly minds. Reading first, second and third day, we think of twenty-four hours. But when Christ was created, the earth had not been created. The sun and the moon had not been created. So did twenty-four hours exist? No.

“But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” This is saying that our time and God's time are not the same. Don't sit down and say God created the earth in seven thousand years. It only means that time with God is different; in that realm, time is not the same.

So to explain it to our human minds, Moses said first day, second day, third day. The best way to understand it is: the first thing God did, the second thing, the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and then the seventh. What came out of the Father's mouth, Christ did. And it had to be given to us in human terms, because the Sabbath is counted from the creation account. If it had been given in God's terms, we would be lost and think every Sabbath comes every thousand years. He rested on the seventh day, so you rest too.

Moses saw these secrets, and God told him to write them but to hide certain things. Unless God's Spirit is in you, you will not understand them, even when they are taught to you.

“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he dwells in eternity. Christ was with him in eternity in the beginning; the Word was with God. Christ did not create everything all at once on the first day. The Lord told him what to do, and he did it. Christ learned from his Father: what he saw his Father do, he was able to do.

“I dwell in the high and holy place”: that is above the heavens, above paradise, the holy of holies, the fourth floor, with restricted access. No man has been up there. He dwells there “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.”

Sirach 18 explains eternity: “The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” In eternity, where the Father is, a thousand years is like nothing. Those are the days of the Ancient of days. Sirach 1:2 says the same: “Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one can count God's days. He exists outside of time, before time.

This goes with what Peter said: the days of Genesis are not earth days. They are measured from where the Father dwells, in eternity.

With a picture of the earth in space on the screen, 2 Esdras 16 was read: “He searcheth the deep, and the treasures thereof; he hath measured the sea, and what it containeth. He hath shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word hath he hanged the earth upon the waters.” All around the earth is space, and the earth hangs in it like an ornament the Lord just hung there. The water it hangs on is space. Astronauts train in the water because that is where they are going; spend too long in space and your bones get brittle, just as they get crushed if you go too deep under water.

Job calls that water something else: “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.” When you see the earth in space, it is on nothing. You cannot see any water, but the water is there surrounding it. The nothing is the water.

So why doesn't the earth move and float off one way or another? That is the Most High showing his power. 2 Esdras 16:59: “He spreadeth out the heavens like a vault; upon the waters hath he founded it.” A vault is an arch; it goes around, it is round, not flat. Founded means established: the earth stays in the spot where he founded it, while the sun moves. This is the same work as Genesis 1:6, where the firmament was set in the midst of the waters.

Balaam, “the man whose eyes are open”, saw the vision of the Almighty and said: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.”

People think these tabernacles are houses. They are our bodies. It is us being that tree by the river, planted by the Lord, beside the living waters. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters”: the waters are poured out from on high, from the Lord, and we will be swimming in those living waters, the waters from heaven above the firmament, not space. “and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” The king is Christ, and that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things were brought out to encourage us. They have been hidden for thousands of years, and understanding them builds up our hope.

Wisdom said her river became a sea. Revelation 15:2: “And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass”. We overcame the white man and his lies, and we stand on that clear water. The Lord divided the waters from the waters above, and the waters above are the wisdom in paradise.

Revelation 22 shows the river of Eden in heaven: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” A river, and the tree of life beside it, just as in the garden.

In Revelation 4, “a door was opened in heaven”, and the voice said, “Come up hither”. John went up into paradise, and that is where those things were shown to him. “And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal”. The sea of glass is the wisdom coming from the throne of God. Esau pictures it as the Bifrost, a bridge leading to paradise.

Psalm 148:4 calls on those waters: “Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” Song of Solomon 4 calls it “a well of living waters”. Christ said he is the living water, and told the woman at the well he would give her living water. Those are the waters above the heavens, the springs up there. The river out of Eden is that same water.

After the waters above the heavens, Sirach 19:19: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” The water that flows out of Eden is wisdom, the knowledge of the commandments, and the one who keeps them eats of the tree of immortality.

Song of Solomon 4 describes the same garden: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Everybody cannot go there. It has an orchard of pomegranates and pleasant fruits, “A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.”

That goes back to Genesis, where the Lord made every tree in the garden to grow that was good for food. The living waters feed the garden, and those who do the commandments receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, which Adam had access to before he sinned.

“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The first is Pison, which compasses the land of Havilah, where there is gold; the second is Gihon, compassing the whole land of Ethiopia; the third is Hiddekel, going toward the east of Assyria; and the fourth is Euphrates. The Most High is doing two things here. It is a similitude of the waters above, since he divided the waters below from the waters above. And it goes into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and that is Adam's governance. It speaks of the heavens, but it came down on the earth too.

Sirach 24 names the same rivers: “He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” These are the four rivers of Genesis, and the water is wisdom and understanding. What went forth through all those rivers was the wisdom of God, going to Adam's sons ruling this earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens, and it is on the earth too.

“The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.” The first man is Adam, and he did not know wisdom perfectly because he sinned. Wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.” The great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.” The best garden is paradise. The brook became a river and the river became a sea, and that sea is the sea of glass in heaven.

“And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”. That is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom comes down from the Father to Christ, it goes to the leaders, and the leaders issue it throughout the earth. “half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.” That means all year round. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth, and Adam is going to be back as king over the earth.

So when Genesis talks about the garden, it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God's glory and wisdom went out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and the other rivers. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions enforcing his laws. His trees were there on the earth too, on earth as it is in heaven. The living waters out of Jerusalem are how it will be again.

Back in Genesis 2:15, “the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and keep it means to rule. Adam ruled the heaven and the earth, and we don't know for how long. He died at 930, but his days only started to be numbered after he sinned. Before that he was immortal, so between Genesis 2 and the temptation in Genesis 3 there could have been hundreds or thousands of years. That is the kingdom of Adam. He had children in the heavens, his firstborn, the twelve tribes, and children on the earth.

2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted”, and Genesis 2:8 says the same thing: “the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” Adam's kingdom ruled the heaven and the earth. The man who could go to paradise, where the Lord is, did not walk around without clothes. Then verse 9: “And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food”. What is that talking about?

Isaiah 61:3: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: us, in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

Reading Genesis 2:9 again: the trees pleasant to the sight and good for food are a similitude for Adam's sons in the heavens, the righteous. “the tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “and the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: that is Satan. The tree people set up and worship in their houses at Christmas references that tree; Babylon referenced it, and Santa Claus is Satan Claus.

God works hand in hand with the prophets. He has Moses write something hard, and he has the other prophets come and explain what it is talking about. Isaiah explains the trees of Genesis: the planting of the Lord is his people.

Psalm 1 was read from the top: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

The man who delights in the law is the tree. He is planted by rivers of water and brings forth fruit. That is what the trees of the garden are: the righteous, the planting of the Lord, bringing forth fruit.

Going back to Genesis 2:9 with that in mind, the trees “pleasant to the sight and good for food” are Adam's sons in the heavens. The rivers of water point to the next verse: “And a river went out of Eden to water the garden”. The trees stand by the river, and that is Adam's governance: the righteous planted by the waters of God's wisdom, in the heavens and on the earth.

Genesis 3:20 is right there in front of our eyes: “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was the mother, bringing forth many children. This was before she fell and before Adam was cast out. The living are children on the earth, created before the fall, and Eve was the mother of them all. Eve was a black woman and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom, not people walking around naked.

2 Esdras 3 shows how many there were: “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” When Adam broke God's law he was cast out of paradise and immortality was taken from him. But there were already nations, tribes, people and kindreds, out of number, so many they could not be counted. For all of that to be around, Adam must have been on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years.

2 Esdras 6:54: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was a lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens. The creatures include the angels, and Adam was over them. “of him come we all”. The words “and the people also whom thou hast chosen” were read as speaking of after the flood, from Noah, because before Noah, and before Adam fell, there were people already. And verse 55: “thou madest the world for our sakes”.

That is how Cain was able to find a wife after he killed Abel. There were many people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. And he was not alone: we were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him. What we read about the future kingdom, governing the nations in angelic bodies, is how it was with Adam. Tobit 8:6 says of Adam and Eve, “of them came mankind”, but that is broad, since all mankind also came from Adam and Eve through Noah's three sons.

Why was Adam told to subdue the earth? Because he lost it. Satan says all the power and glory of this earth was given to him, and he can give it to whoever he wants. Adam lost rulership of the earth, so now he has to come and subdue it again, and kill Satan.

“And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Cain was not created in Adam's image. She said she got a man, and we keep reading about the children of men; his very name tells you he was not created in Adam's image or after his likeness. “And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Cain killed Abel. Abel was righteous and Cain was wicked, and Abel was supposed to be the righteous child created in Adam's image.

So what did the Lord do? Genesis 4 and 5 are the replenishing of the earth, filling it again with the righteous seed, his sons. Genesis 2 goes into Adam's rulership, Genesis 2 and 3 are the same as Ezekiel 31, Adam's rule and his fall, and Genesis 4 and 5 are Adam and Eve replenishing the earth after the fall.

Genesis 5: “This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”. Adam means from the ground. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Now the sons of God, the children above, start being sent down to the earth and born through Adam and his descendants. The twelve tribes are born into the earth through him. Seth's whole lineage is the sons of God, Israel, born in the image of God. Cain was not.

The command to replenish the earth and subdue it is not finished. The earth has not yet been subdued, and that waits for the kingdom.

“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

Revelation 13:5 says “there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies”, and Daniel 7:25 says the same: “he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Revelation 13:7 adds that “it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. The great words are things like the image of Cesare Borgia as Christ, a white man dying for the sins of everybody on the planet, getting dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas, December 25th and the rest. To wear out the saints is slavery.

“and think to change times and laws”. They changed the time with daylight saving time. They moved the beginning of the year from spring to January. Genesis 1:14 was read to show something else they changed: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”.

Leviticus 23 shows what the seasons are for: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” The Sabbath is listed first, and it is all year round. Then come the seasonal holidays: Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the spring; the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth; Pentecost, counting fifty days; the blowing of trumpets on the first day of the seventh month, the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth of the seventh month; and the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth.

Sirach 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The declaration of times is the high holy days. The lights God set in the heaven keep his calendar, and that is the calendar the beast thought to change.

“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” The greater light is the sun and the lesser light is the moon. Notice the wording: great lights. He did not make a quarter moon or half a light. He made two great lights. What they call the full moon today is actually the new moon, and many cultures, like the Maya, hold full moon gatherings. Deuteronomy 33:14 speaks of Joseph's land and “the precious things put forth by the moon”, things that come out when the moon is at its peak, like the coquí frogs that come out under the moonlight in the islands where Ephraim and Manasseh dwell.

Sirach 43 goes on: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”. The word month comes from moon. Every feast starts at the new moon in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom. The armies above are the armies of Revelation 19: “the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses”.

The moon is “a sign of the world”. The full moon stands for when we were in our full power and understanding. As it wanes and goes dark, that is us going into captivity, into full darkness, and when it comes back to fullness, that is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. Isaiah 60:2: “the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. When you see the dark moon, that is what it represents: we lost our heritage, and darkness covers the world.

Psalm 82 shows why: “How long will ye judge unjustly”, and because of it, “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Even the lights are out of course because of our sins. The seasons are out of order, and if the Sabbath comes every seven days, a month should have twenty-eight days. Isaiah 30:26 shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases, so in the kingdom the moon will not go back into darkness. Binding up the breach is gathering the twelve tribes again, as Amos 9:11 says: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”.
“Observe the month of Abib, and keep the passover.” The first month, when Passover falls, is named Abib, the spring month, so the true new year begins in spring, not in January.

The month God made the beginning of months is the month Israel came out of Egypt. Moses says, “Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt”, and that month is Abib, the spring month, not January.

After Exodus 4:22, 1 John 3:1 confirms it: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”. We who? We Israelites. The sons of God of Genesis 6 are not angels; they are us.

So Genesis 6 is about our fathers: “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Our sons became famous men. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” The man God was angry with was the sons of God. Once we broke the laws we already had and went in unto the daughters of men, our kids turned into the devil and started acting like the devil on the planet. That is why God had to bring the flood.

Psalm 82:6-7 says of us: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” The flood came and we all died, and we came back through Noah's son Shem. And we still have not learned our lesson. Today the same snares catch our men and women who leave their own people for other nations, and it costs them everything.

Psalm 82 opens: “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” We are the mighty and we are the gods. Then: “How long will ye judge unjustly”? What did we do? Genesis 6:1 tells it: “And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them”. Nations were beginning to form on the earth. Then verse 2 speaks of “the sons of God”.

Who are the sons of God? Exodus 4:22: “And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Now we know who the sons of God are. It is not talking about angels; it is talking about us, before we were called Israel. Before the flood, we were called the sons of God.

“That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” We started taking wives of the other nations, and there were laws on that. Deuteronomy 7:3-4: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”, “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Joshua 23:13 warns that such nations “shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes”. Tobit 4:12 says to “take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”, for “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children”.

That was how we judged unjustly and accepted the persons of the wicked. God's son, his firstborn, broke the law he already had, and the Lord said, “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” He cut down our lifespan.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All creation is waiting for the sons of God, Israel, to be revealed. The sons of God fell in Genesis 6 by judging unjustly, but the plan still stands.

Psalm 82:8: “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.” Psalm 2:8 says to Christ: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” And we are joint heirs: Romans 8:17, “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. What Christ gets, he gives to us. Revelation 2:26-27: “to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”, “even as I received of my Father.”

Christ has made us “kings and priests” (Revelation 1:6), and Paul says, “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The saints are the children of Israel, as Psalm 148:14 says. “Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we will judge are not Michael or Gabriel; they are each other, the twelve tribes, as Christ promised the twelve would sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

That is the manifestation creation is waiting for. We may look like nobody now, but in time we will rule the nations with Christ. All we have to do is endure to the end.
Judas sent a sin offering for the dead, “mindful of the resurrection”. That is how the old ways thought the resurrection was reached, one more of the principles we leave to go on unto perfection.

Water washing began with the priests: “Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat”. John the Baptist did not make it up; it was one of the old ordinances we leave behind to go on unto perfection.
The principles we are told to leave include “divers washings, and carnal ordinances”, which stood only until the time of reformation. They were never meant to last, so we go on unto perfection.
Washing was only ever a symbol. Even with “much soap”, God says “thine iniquity is marked before me”, so water could never make anyone perfect, and the doctrine of baptisms is left behind.

“When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”, Esau, seeing “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, went his own rebellious way anyway. “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling, and that is where the light-skinned Arabs come from.

Jacob went toward Haran, and at a certain place he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, “and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” The Lord promised, “the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. That is all four corners: before they were even born, it was prophesied that Jacob’s seed would be found in the four corners of the earth, scattered among the families of the earth, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” And the Lord promised, “I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven”, a portal to paradise. He set up his stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” He vowed the tenth, the tithe.

Keep Bethel in mind. On the map it sits right under Shechem, the place where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan and where Rehoboam was later crowned. These early holy places all lay in the land that would become Ephraim’s.

The division between Ephraim and Judah did not begin at the split of the kingdom; it was building long before. Part of it goes back to Joseph, the father of Ephraim.

Joseph was raised up to tell Pharaoh what was coming: “Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land”, and “it shall be very grievous”. “And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.” Joseph prophesied the famine and showed Egypt how to prepare for it, and by it Israel was saved when Jacob and his sons ran down to Egypt.

The same pattern ran through Abraham. After the Lord told him, “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house”, he came from Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates, up to Haran, and down into Canaan, the stretch called the Fertile Crescent. When famine struck Canaan, Abraham ran to Egypt too, just as Jacob and his house later did. The parallels line up.

So Joseph’s house carried a great deal: Joseph saved Israel in the famine, and later Joshua, of Ephraim, divided the land. That is part of why Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and why the rivalry that tore the kingdom in two was already there long before Rehoboam.

“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.
blog/2026/2026-01-31-2026-01-31-my-templ: God gave a law of the beasts to make a difference between the clean and the unclean. So “every creature” being good means good for its purpose, not good to eat; pork stays unclean no matter who prays over it.
Meats are received by those who believe and know the truth, and “thy law is the truth”. So what makes the meat clean is the word of the law, not a prayer said over a plate of pork.
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment.” Truly believing means keeping the law about clean and unclean meats, not departing from the faith by eating whatever you like.

Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.
blog/2026/2026-02-01-2026-02-01-the-divi: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar.” Loving God and loving your brother go hand in hand, so whoever hates his own people is still in darkness: God and race.
The new commandment John writes is the one Christ gave: “love one another”. That love is how all men know his disciples, and the one who loves his brother abides in the light.

“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart” was already in the law, so Christ's new commandment is the old one Israel had from the beginning but was not following. Bear no grudge against your own people; love them.
The old commandment from the beginning is the greatest: “Hear, O Israel”, love the Lord with all your heart, and “love thy neighbour as thyself”. Love your people, love your ways.

At Bethel the Lord promised Jacob, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. Israel would be everywhere on the earth, through captivity and through migration, forced or willing. And the promise goes on, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: that is the Israelite families in those lands, north, south, east and west. The nations are not the ones blessed; their blessing is servitude.

Then the Lord renamed him: “Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”. “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”. In context that can mean all twelve tribes, but prophetically it is written that way for the division to come: the nation is the southern kingdom, Judah, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom, Ephraim. The kings out of his loins are Saul, David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

Moses shows where the division came from. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” He kept us “as the apple of his eye.” “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”, rich, comfortable and rebellious, and “lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”, which is Christ. So the Lord said, “I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Isaiah names who is not a people: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people”, after the northern kingdom joined Syria against Judah.

Hosea says the same of the company of nations: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Ephraim became as Gentiles, heathens, the uncircumcision. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Yet the number of Israel “shall be as the sand of the sea”, as promised to Jacob, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”, and that head is Christ. Ezekiel agrees: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The hatred between the nation and the company of nations is why both fell, the north first and Judah after. The law always said, “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, and “he that hateth his brother is in darkness”. Esau never forgets and holds his grudges, while Jacob in captivity forgets his own and cares more for his oppressor. Love your people and love your ways, and the nation and the company of nations become one again.
