blog/2026/2026-02-08-2026-02-08-edom-s-a:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

Paul speaks of the man of sin: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”. His coming is after the working of Satan, meaning Satan is his father, as he was Cain’s. That is Esau, Cain come again.

Genesis 3:15 ends, “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Christ is our head, smitten so that the sheep were scattered. But the heel is Edom’s Achilles heel. Jacob took hold of Esau’s heel at birth, and in Daniel 2 “a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.”

The image is the empires. The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon; the silver is Persia and Media; the brass is Greece, “which shall bear rule over all the earth.” That was Alexander, “son of Philip, the Macedonian”, who “slew the kings of the earth” until “the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up”: the beginning of white supremacy in the earth. His kingdom was parted among his generals, “and evils were multiplied in the earth.” Their own books, The Chronology of Ancient Nations and The Rise of Christendom, trace Philip back to Esau. The iron is Rome, and we are still in it: America and NATO, a kingdom “partly strong, and partly broken”, strong in military, with the toes as the European nations. The miry clay is the melting pot: “they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”.

The stone is Christ, “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He strikes the image on its feet, its heel, and “the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” And “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. We are living in the days of these kings. What we teach is the beginning of that kingdom, and it cannot be stopped; it will consume all these kingdoms with the word of God.

In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.
blog/2026/2026-02-14-2026-02-14-fighting:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” “And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.”

Abraham was not circumcised on the eighth day after he was born; he was ninety-nine. Ishmael was thirteen. There was no eighth day, no days of purifying and no sacrifice. That is circumcision of the fathers, not circumcision after the manner of Moses.

The Pharisees wanted circumcision and sacrifice together, after the manner of Moses, because sacrificing was their bread and butter. As more people followed Christ, more of them stopped sacrificing, and if the people stop sacrificing, the Pharisees cannot eat. So they went into the churches saying you have to be circumcised to be saved. That is not what the Bible, Christ or the apostles taught. They were trying to put back on the people the yoke that could not be borne, the same one Peter asked about: “why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?”

“And the Lord visited Sarah as he had said”, and “Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.” Sarah conceived in old age and Abraham named the child Isaac. Then: “And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac being eight days old, as God had commanded him.” “And Abraham was an hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.”

When Joseph’s brothers sat down to eat bread, they saw “a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.” Judah said, “What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites.” Then the verse changes names: “Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.”

There are always questions about the Midianites and the Ishmaelites. Genesis 25 shows who the Midianites were: “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah. And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.” Keturah had six sons by Abraham, and Midian is one of them. The chapter goes on to his sons: “And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.”

So the Midianites are Abraham’s children through Keturah, just as the Ishmaelites are Abraham’s children through Hagar. They were working together and roaming the land together, all Abraham’s kids, and they looked very similar. That is why the story says Ishmaelites, then Midianites, then “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar,” and then in Genesis 39 Potiphar “bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” It is not a contradiction; these groups were together.

Genesis 37 names both groups in the sale of Joseph: the Midianites drew him out of the pit and “sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver,” and later “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar.” Genesis 25:12 shows who the Ishmaelites were: “Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham.”

Abraham had Ishmael from Hagar, and Ishmael had sons as well: Nebajoth the firstborn, “and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.” “These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.”

Abraham’s children from Keturah and Abraham’s children from Hagar always lived together and worked together. So when a company of Ishmaelites comes by carrying spices down to Egypt and Midianite merchantmen are among them, it is one caravan of Abraham’s other children traveling side by side.

Meanwhile the brothers, so envious of Joseph, dipped his coat of many colours in the blood of a kid of the goats and let Jacob believe “an evil beast hath devoured him.” Reuben had suggested the pit so he could come back and save him, and when he returned, “Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.” Envy will have you do evil things. Remember Reuben’s character; it plays a part later.

Joseph was seventeen, a teenager, sold into Egypt: “Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” Yet “the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master “saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand,” and made him overseer over his house, putting all that he had into his hand.

Luke 16:10 explains why: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” Joseph was in slavery, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up.

It speaks to us today. Many brothers and sisters have jobs, and the Most High is observing us in whatever we do. The least that we are faithful in is these little jobs out here. Just as Joseph was in captivity, we are in captivity, but that does not mean we can steal, lie or rob. When you are on your jobs, do not steal; deal right. God is watching each and every one of us.

And look what faithfulness brought: “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.” The theme is the same as when Jacob worked for Laban all those years and Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake. Faithful in little, Joseph was trusted with much, until his master “knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat.”

When Potiphar’s wife could not get her way, she lied. She called the men of her house and said, “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.” Then “she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home”: she kept his clothes as false evidence, and told her husband the same lie.

Sirach shows what that kind of tongue does: “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction. Joseph was the greatest man in Potiphar's house, trusted with everything, and a lying tongue brought him down to the king's prison.

Others are in jail because a woman started a fight and expected him to defend her. Don't deal with a woman like that; that is the kind of woman Joseph had over him.

She told her husband, “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me,” and “when his master heard the words of his wife,” “his wrath was kindled.” On nothing but her word, “Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember how old Joseph is here: 17.

That is how our people have fallen too: brothers in prison on a lie, and in slavery times men like Emmett Till put to death because of a lying woman's words. More have fallen by the tongue than by the sword. Guard yourself from the kind of company that can destroy you with a word.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Make not haste means don't leave this truth in your time of trouble. Satan will tell you, if you weren't in that Bible you wouldn't be going through half of what you're going through; you had it better when you served me. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Joseph's family was rich; Jacob was a wealthy man. Joseph was taken from all that, sold as a slave, and now he is in the midst of poverty, in prison, for a crime he refused to commit. That is a low estate, and he bore it without leaving God.

Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph. Israel today has been brought down to a low estate, and the tests and trials come because we serve the Lord. Endure them, cleave unto him, and you will be increased at your last end, as Joseph was.

Even in prison, “the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.” The keeper “committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison,” and “looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.”

Solomon gives the reason: “When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Joseph. He was a Hebrew slave, accused of attacking his master's wife, locked in the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and his very jailer became favourable to him and handed him the whole prison.

It is the same pattern all through Joseph's life: in Potiphar's house the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house “for Joseph’s sake,” just as Laban was blessed for Jacob's sake when Jacob worked for him. Joseph's ways pleased the Lord; he refused sin even when it cost him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it to prosper. Keep your ways pleasing to God, and he will make even those set over you in captivity to be at peace with you.

Potiphar’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” Joseph refused, and he did not refuse half-heartedly: “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Notice he was not blaming God that he was a slave in a strange land. His master had kept nothing back from him “but thee, because thou art his wife,” and Joseph would not touch her.

This was not a single moment. “she spake to Joseph day by day”; she was trying to wear him down day by day. And the Egyptians loved beautiful women; remember when Abraham went down into Egypt, Sarah was in danger because of her beauty. Potiphar’s wife was no ugly woman; she was good on the eyes, and Joseph, at 17 years old, still said no. When she finally “caught him by his garment,” “he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.”

Sirach gives the precept for what Joseph did: “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” Joseph saw sin like a snake, and he ran like a rabbit. If a snake fell into the room right now, everybody would be out of there. That snake is your sin. “All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.”

Everybody's demon is not the same. For some it is food; for most of the brothers it is sexual demons, and those demons will get you. Put yourself in Joseph's place and be honest about it: many have been put out for adultery two and three times. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did: don't stand there and reason with it, don't come near it. Flee.

The butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord and were put in ward “the place where Joseph was bound.” “they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night,” and in the morning they were sad, because “there is no interpreter of it.” Joseph answered, “Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.”

Sirach speaks to dreams: “The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.” “Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.” Don't chase dreams; a man who lives by every dream is grasping at shadows.

But verse 3 gives a clue to understanding the dreams that come from God: “The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” You may dream about somebody you know, say a man named Joe, and see Joe's face; but it is not Joe. It is someone similar to Joe, maybe in age or in what they do for a living. It could be Bob. You just have to know the people in your circle.

That is how the dreams in Genesis 40 work. The butler's vine with “three branches” and the baker's “three white baskets” were resemblances of one thing to another: the three branches and the three baskets were three days. The interpretation belonged to God, and Joseph gave it.

Jeremiah says the same thing Job said: “Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.” Two prophets, and neither one blessed the day of his birth. Put that together with Pharaoh's birthday in Genesis 40, where the baker was hanged at the feast.

We never celebrated birthdays. They are days of narcissism, days to put ourselves up above God. The custom came from the nations; it came through the white man, who got it from what they dug up in their archaeological digs, and then taught that we should be celebrating birthdays.

So stop celebrating that foolishness, even with the excuse that it's for the children. It is not of God. And after that birthday feast, “Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.”

Joseph's interpretations came to pass “the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants.” On that birthday “he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again,” “But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.”

Wherever you read of a birthday in scripture, Pharaoh's birthday, Herod's birthday, the birthday of one of the Greek kings, something bad happens. Here a man is hanged at a birthday feast. A birthday is a day of narcissism, a day of proclaiming yourself to be God.

Job shows how the Hebrews felt about the day of their birth: “Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.” A righteous man did not exalt the day he was born; he wished it would perish. That is why we never celebrated birthdays.

After interpreting the butler's dream, Joseph asked him, “think on me when it shall be well with thee,” and “make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:” “For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.” He wanted out of that dungeon.

Notice the prison is called a dungeon. Lamentations uses the same word: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” To cast a stone upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity.

That goes with our political prisoners, who have been in there for a long time, cut off in the dungeon with a stone cast over them. Joseph, stolen away and imprisoned though he had done nothing, is a picture of his people in captivity.

“at the end of two full years” Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat kine eaten up by seven lean kine, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears “blasted with the east wind.” None of the magicians could interpret it, until the chief butler remembered his faults and told Pharaoh of the young Hebrew. “Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.”

To every problem, brothers, we must have a solution. Some spirits among us have a problem for every solution; stay away from brothers and sisters like that.

This is why you see Israel today meeting dignitaries across the world: because we have been diligent in God's business. Mean men are obscure men, bums on the internet with a handful of followers who want to debate you for clout, whose numbers go up as soon as they see the shirt. They are not worth your time. Proverbs says “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings,” and Paul shows which business that is: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” That is the proof. The business is God's business, serving the Lord, and you must not be slothful when it comes to it.

So don't be over there asleep in the things of God. Be fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, and God will set you before kings and not before mean men, as he did Joseph.

Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

blog/2026/2026-07-19-2026-07-19-drowning:
Paul beseeches the brethren “by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That “him” is Christ, and Genesis 49:10 shows why: “unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” He is the only one who can gather all twelve tribes together. When people on earth say they are the ones Christ is using to gather the twelve tribes, don't listen to that.

Jacob's blessing lays it out. “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the sceptre is the kingship. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: between the feet means the loins, the seed. The lawgiver comes out of Judah's loins, which shows there is no immaculate conception. “until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes.

That is why Paul tells them “be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled.” In his time many were running around saying the resurrection had come and gone already. Paul reminds them not to let anyone deceive them; Christ had not returned, and the gathering belongs to him alone, when he comes.

Paul says “that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” The falling away is not people leaving Christianity to join Islam, the way Christians read it. The falling away means the twelve tribes of Israel have to fall and go into captivity, and Luke 21:24 shows it.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “and shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem taken over by other nations, in particular the Edomite nations, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until that time of rulership is over.

So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all twelve tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed, the son of perdition. Perdition means eternal damnation, spiritual ruin and hell; it comes from the Latin perdere, to destroy or to lose. It is the fate of the wicked, the absolute loss of one's soul, the final loss of salvation and unending punishment.

The Lord shall consume that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth”, and 2 Esdras 13 shows the Son doing it: “this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest.”

Those wicked inventions are the ICBM missiles and all that technology, their satellites spread across the globe. Christ will rebuke all of it and “shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame.”

Then: “he shall destroy them without labour by the law.” He will not need their weapons; the law does the destroying. God is saying his law is fire, the same fire that is in the mouth of those who teach it. That is the spirit of his mouth and “the brightness of his coming” that destroys the Wicked in 2 Thessalonians 2.

Paul says the Wicked's “coming is after the working of Satan.” Our comings are supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings are after Satan, and that goes back to Genesis 4.

The Lord speaks to Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Then the speech switches. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: now he is talking to Satan. Cain's desire shall be unto Satan, “and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over Cain.

So from the beginning Cain was put under Satan's rule, and his line has walked after Satan ever since. That is why the coming of the man of sin is “after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: he is following the one who was set to rule over his father.

“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” This is the same power Paul describes when the Lord consumes that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” God's word is the fire and the hammer.

We have to believe that. Sometimes we only believe what we can see. The Lord said the angels are all around us; we just don't see them. In the same way, we don't see the word working in the spirit, but it is working. When it is spoken it breaks the rock in pieces, whether the hearer receives it or not.

That is why we must use God's word and not our own eloquence. Those who reject it are condemned by it, and when Christ comes, that same word destroys the Wicked by the brightness of his coming.

Paul says the Wicked shall be revealed, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of God's mouth is the holy Bible, and Jeremiah 5:14 shows how it consumes: “behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.”

Some of us speak very well and have eloquent words, and that is fine, but we must use God's word; that is where the power is. We read the Bible but don't see the spiritual effect it has in this realm, because our eyes are closed. God is saying, my word is fire. Speak it whether they hear or forbear. Even those who reject it are at home tossing and tumbling in their beds, because the way it is broken down haunts them.

As we teach the word of God, we are judging, and many are being marked for death. Everyone who hears it and rejects it and refuses it: remember that Christ said it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah than for those who do not hear his messengers. The words are the fire, the people who reject them are the wood, and that is how the Lord consumes the wicked with the spirit of his mouth.

Christ said this to the Pharisees, who were so in love with Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The lusts are the desires; they will do whatever their father desires.

“He was a murderer from the beginning”: that is Cain, not the spiritual demon. Cain murdered Abel. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.” Cain is a liar and the father of lies. Why? Because Satan is his father; Satan is his daddy.

This ties to Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and to 2 Thessalonians 2:9, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.” The line of Cain comes and goes after Satan, murdering and lying, just as their father did.

The Wicked comes “with all power and signs and lying wonders”, and Christ warned of the same: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.”

The great signs and wonders go with their science and their technology. Something major is going to happen. No one knows when, but before this kingdom goes down there is going to be a worldwide event to deceive the world, and some of us, God forbid, will be deceived by it.

That is why we must hold to God's word. The lying wonders come after the working of Satan, and only the word, the fire in our mouths, will keep us from being taken in when they come.

“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That is Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and it is 2 Thessalonians 2, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.”

The wicked man has Satan standing at his right hand, and he follows everything Satan says. That is why his coming is with “all power and signs and lying wonders”: it is Satan's working carried out through the man he rules.

So the scriptures line up from the beginning to the end: Cain under Satan's rule, the Pharisees doing the lusts of their father the devil, and the man of sin coming after the working of Satan, until the Lord consumes him with the spirit of his mouth.

Revelation 13 describes the same working Paul does: “he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men.” That fire coming down from heaven is thermonuclear fire.

“And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do.” See what it calls them: miracles. Those are the signs and wonders. It says the same thing Matthew 24 says and 2 Thessalonians 2 says, “signs and lying wonders”, only with a different word.

So the Wicked's coming after the working of Satan shows up as their science and their weapons, fire from heaven that looks like miracles, used to deceive the world. The Lord will consume him with the spirit of his mouth and destroy him with the brightness of his coming.

blog/2026/2026-07-25-2026-07-25-the-reli:
The Lord told Ezekiel, “set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” Who or what is mount Seir? Genesis 36 answers: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” Esau's dwelling is Seir, so when the Bible prophesies against Seir, it is prophesying against Esau, the nation of Edom. When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: all the other nations sit between those two. They are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. The story is Jacob and Esau. Christians do not know what that means at all.

Rebekah bore twins, but they were not identical, because the Lord said “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” They looked different. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau means wasted away: his melanin was wasted away. Look at them in a heat wave in France: when they are in the sun they get red. Down south they are called rednecks, but it is not just their necks. Don't call them white; they are Esau, and these are his children.

The scripture never mentions Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father. In fact, Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. Genesis 2:7 shows what that was: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” The dust of the ground is different shades of brown, and the deeper you dig, the darker it gets. That is what Adam looked like, and Eve, and everyone who came from them.

The only one who differed was Esau, and that is why the scribes had to write down his color: he was starkly different. In the old world, Cain's line was cursed with a lack of melanin. The flood came and killed them all off, and God brought them all back through Noah's three sons.

So when you move up the generations to Isaac and Rebekah, the two lines return in one womb. Esau is the return of Cain's lineage, and Jacob is the return of Seth. That is why the two boys were two manner of people from birth: Esau the cunning hunter, a man of the field who liked the rush of the hunt, and Jacob a plain man, dwelling in tents, herding the sheep and the goats.

Esau cried, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” Jacob had already received the major blessing. Rebekah sent him in, dressed in goats' hair so he would feel hairy like his brother, because she remembered what God told her at the birth: the elder shall serve the younger. When Jacob feared a curse, she said let it fall on her. Christians teach that Jacob was the evil son and Esau the good one, and black people in church echo it. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicator, the one who despised his birthright, and Rebekah was being obedient to God.

Isaac answered Esau: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” Dew falls everywhere, and wherever it falls, Esau would live; he would have the best places on the planet. How would he get them? “And by thy sword shalt thou live”: by war. God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, the same blessing Cain's line had when Tubal-cain made all kinds of weapons.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” When did that first happen? 2 Kings 8 answers. “Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign”, and “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.” Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David's sake. “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” That is the first time Esau broke the yoke from off his neck, just as Genesis 27:40 prophesied.

After that, Edom turned on his brother outright. When the Babylonians destroyed the first temple in 586 BCE, Edom helped them instead of helping Judah: rejoicing, looting the city, blocking the survivors who fled. Obadiah, “concerning Edom”, says, “even thou wast as one of them”, and “Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape.” 1 Esdras names who set the fire: “the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

Hebrews calls Esau a “fornicator, or profane person”, and brothers often ask what that means. The scriptures explain it, beginning with his marriages: “Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.” His parents did not like his choice of those Hittite women.

Some unlearned Israelites use these two verses to say Esau was black, because his children were mixed with the Hittites. No. God kept that line the way it is. Even today, no matter how black you are, if you marry a white woman you can tell the child is a hybrid: high yellow, sometimes yellow hair, green eyes. Look at Drake as a boy with his family: his hair is like his father's, but his complexion is closer to his mother's.

So are we to believe that back then God could not keep that same lighter red complexion in Esau's line? These hybrid children look more like Esau. Mixing with the Hittites did not make Esau black; it is part of what made him a fornicator.

After the Hittite wives, Esau went further: “Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father; Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.”

Esau saw that his marrying the daughters of Canaan angered Isaac, and instead of turning back to his own kindred, he went to Ishmael. So now he married Arab kids too. That is what Esau was doing: taking wives outside his father's tribe, one after another.

That is the fornication Hebrews 12:16 names. Esau married the Hittites and the Ishmaelites, strange women, and he was profane because for “one morsel of meat” he sold his birthright; it meant a lot, and he did not care about it.

Tobit 4:12 shows why Esau is called a fornicator: “Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe.” Whoredom falls under fornication. Esau married Hittite women and Ishmaelite women, strange women not of his father's tribe.

Ishmael was the beginning of another race; Genesis is the beginning of races. Tobit goes on: “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

So the fathers married within their own kindred and were blessed in their children; Esau did not. Then there is the profaneness. Hebrews says he sold his birthright “for one morsel of meat”, and that shows what was in the pottage. When Esau came in from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”, he wanted it as it was, raw, red and bloody. “therefore was his name called Edom”, which means red. He said, “Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?” and “thus Esau despised his birthright.” And there are brothers today lusting after these same people and having children with them.

That is why, “when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected”: rejected by God, “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”
God is a witness “against the adulterers”, like couples who swap partners. His law says the man and the woman “shall both of them die”, for “so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.”

God will be “a swift witness against the sorcerers”, for his law says, “Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.” Witchcraft dressed up as spirituality or crystals is still witchcraft, and he has not changed.
God stands with “the widow, and the fatherless.” His law says, “Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child”, and when they cry, “I will surely hear their cry”, and his wrath waxes hot.
God stands against “false swearers”, for his law says, “ye shall not swear by my name falsely.” Lying under oath, perjury and false statements are what he will be a swift witness against.

Those who “oppress the hireling in his wages” break the law: “the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night.” Paying brothers late or unequally, even among us, is that oppression.

The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

Some argue there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.
