Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

Judah’s line held men of great wisdom: Zarah’s sons Ethan, Heman, Chalcol and Darda were so wise that Solomon is measured against them. He was “wiser than all men”, surpassing even the wise men of his own tribe.

Amminadab’s daughter Elisheba, sister of Nahshon, married Aaron, so priests and kings intermarried. That is why Eleazar the high priest had a mother of Judah, and why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.
“Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah” was also “captain of the children of Judah.” These were princes and captains, not ordinary men, and Boaz came from that line.

About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.
The trees “shall overshadow Israel” because “God shall lead Israel with joy”. Overshadow means to lead, so the Highest overshadowing Mary was the Lord leading her way.
A woman who “have conceived seed” conceives through her husband. So “thou shalt conceive in thy womb” uses the same plain language of seed and birth.
Mary asked “How shall this be”, for “how can a man then understand his own way”? The Lord guided her steps, as he guides every one of us.
The words “conceive in thy womb” speak of conception as it always happens: when Boaz went in unto Ruth, “the Lord gave her conception”. To conceive takes seed, and the Lord gives it.

To overshadow is to lead, guide and defend, like “a cloud shadowing the camp” as Israel crossed the sea. So “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee” means the Lord would guide Mary to her husband.

Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.
